groups.title: How tRPC eliminates the client-server type boundary
groups.question: In your T3 app you rename a field on the server and the client code immediately shows a type error, without any generated client or schema file. Explain how tRPC makes this happen and how it treats input from the client.

followUps.tRPC's type inference: how server types: How do server types reach the client in tRPC without a code generation step?
followUps.Zod input schemas in tRPC procedures: pa: Types already describe the input, so why does a procedure also need a Zod schema?

evidence.text: The server exports the type of its router.
The client imports it as a type only, so no server code is shipped to the browser.
TypeScript infers each procedure's input and output types from that router type.

notEnough: Only saying tRPC is end-to-end typesafe.

misconceptions.text: Says tRPC sends the server's types to the browser at runtime.

evidence.text: Data arriving at the server can come from anyone, so it cannot be trusted just because of types.
The input schema validates the data before the procedure runs.
Invalid input is rejected with a bad request error that the client can show.

groups.title: tRPC middleware and context for auth and request data
groups.question: Many procedures need the current user and the database, and some must only be used by signed-in users. Explain how context and middleware handle this in tRPC.

followUps.Context: passing the session and databas: What goes into tRPC context and why is it created per request?
followUps.Protected procedures with tRPC middlewar: How does a protectedProcedure make sure no one forgets an auth check?

evidence.text: Context is built for each request.
It typically holds the session and the database client.
Every procedure receives it, so none needs to import or rebuild these itself.

notEnough: Only saying context is shared data.

evidence.text: A middleware checks the session before the procedure runs.
If there is no session it throws an unauthorized error.
Building procedures from protectedProcedure applies the check automatically every time.

notEnough: Only saying it checks if the user is logged in.

groups.title: Defining tRPC routers and procedures
groups.question: Your tRPC router has grown to fifty procedures in one file covering posts, users and comments. Explain how you would organize it and choose between queries and mutations.

followUps.Queries versus mutations: when to use ea: What is the difference between a query and a mutation, and why does it matter on the client?
followUps.Merging routers: splitting tRPC into fea: How would you split the router by feature and how does the client call a nested procedure?

evidence.text: Queries read data and mutations change it.
Queries are cached and can be refetched automatically by TanStack Query.
Mutations run only when called and are not cached.

notEnough: Only saying queries get and mutations post.

evidence.text: Each feature gets its own router, such as posts, users and comments.
They are combined into one root router.
The client calls them through matching nested names, like posts.list.

notEnough: Only saying you split the file.

groups.title: Using tRPC on the client with TanStack Query
groups.question: On the client you show a list of posts and a form that creates a post, and after creating one the list does not update. Explain how the tRPC client hooks work and how you would fix the list.

followUps.useQuery and useMutation hooks generated: What do the tRPC useQuery and useMutation hooks give you?
followUps.Cache invalidation after mutations with: After creating a post, how do you make the post list refresh?

evidence.text: They are typed wrappers around TanStack Query's hooks.
useQuery returns the data plus loading and error state.
useMutation returns a function to trigger the change and its pending state.
In the mutation's success callback, invalidate the list query.
That marks the cached list as stale.
The list is refetched in the background, so it shows the new post without a page reload.
